purpose: lighthouse proves a FEATURE branch works before it merges into its core branch, by running the project's suite on both branches, driving the running product, rechecking the surfaces next to the change and computing a verdict.

objectives.text: Every run ends in a computed verdict.
The project's suite runs on both branches.
Each neighbour is rechecked on both builds.
What a run costs in time and money.

run.start.description: lighthouse launch began a run, written before it starts the child session.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
questions: When did the run start, and which run of a harness started it?
Which branches and options was the run given?

core.description: The core branch the run compares against.
core.measured_from: The --core flag lighthouse launch was given.
core.excludes: The commit, which the summary's core_commit records.
core.reading: A name identifies the branch; null means unknown.
core.question: Which core branch was the run proving against?

feature.description: The FEATURE branch the run proves.
feature.measured_from: The --feature flag lighthouse launch was given.
feature.excludes: The commit, which the summary's feature_commit records.
feature.reading: A name identifies the branch; null means unknown.
feature.question: Which FEATURE branch was the run proving?

results.measured_from: The --results flag lighthouse launch was given, resolved.
results.includes: The folder the child session works and writes in.
results.reading: A path names the folder; null means unknown.
results.question: Where are the run's working files?

retest.description: Whether the run retests from previous results.
retest.includes: Runs given a previous results folder.
retest.reading: true means a retest; false means a fresh run; null means unknown.
retest.question: How often does a run retest from earlier results?

final.description: Whether the run was the final one before opening the pull request.
final.reading: true means the run was final; false means it was not; null means unknown.
final.question: How often is a run the final one?

spec.description: Whether the run was given a spec to read.
spec.reading: true means a spec was given; false means none was; null means unknown.
spec.question: How often does a run have a spec?

run.end.description: The run's child session ended, written by lighthouse launch before the summary.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
questions: How did the run end and how long did it take?
Which caller messages fall inside the run's span?

verdict.measured_from: The verdict line lighthouse launch prints: the child's last verdict line, or launch's own blocked line.
verdict.includes: One of green, failures, blocked or unproven.
verdict.excludes: Any opinion beyond the computed verdict.
verdict.reading: green means proven with no failure; failures means at least one confirmed failure; blocked means the run stopped; unproven means the new behaviour was not shown; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
verdict.question: How do runs end?

child_exit.measured_from: The exit status of the claude -p child session lighthouse launch started.
child_exit.includes: The code the child process returned.
child_exit.reading: 0 means the child exited normally; any other value is the code it gave; null means the child never started.
child_exit.question: How often does the child session exit abnormally?

run_seconds.description: How long the run took from run.start to run.end.
run_seconds.measured_from: The time of run.end minus the time of run.start, as launch took them.
run_seconds.includes: The whole child session and launch's own work before and after it.
run_seconds.excludes: The caller's work before launch started and after it ended.
run_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
run_seconds.question: How long does a lighthouse run take?

summary.description: One line per lighthouse run: its verdict, the suite on both builds, every product path, the build result and lighthouse's own spend, priced at write time. Order runs and state periods by started, never the envelope ts, which for an imported summary is the import's time.

started.measured_from: The time lighthouse launch took when it appended run.start.
started.reading: A later time means later; order runs and state periods by started, never the envelope ts; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
started.question: When did the run start, and which runs fall in a period?

ended.measured_from: The time lighthouse launch took when it appended run.end, after the child session ended.
ended.reading: A later time means later; order runs and state periods by started, never the envelope ts; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
ended.question: When did the run end?

run_seconds.description: How long the run took from run.start to run.end.
run_seconds.measured_from: The time of run.end minus the time of run.start, as launch took them.
run_seconds.includes: The whole child session and launch's own work before and after it.
run_seconds.excludes: The caller's work before launch started and after it ended.
run_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
run_seconds.question: How long does a lighthouse run take?

verdict.measured_from: The verdict line lighthouse launch prints: the child's last verdict line, or launch's own blocked line.
verdict.includes: One of green, failures, blocked or unproven.
verdict.excludes: Any opinion beyond the computed verdict.
verdict.reading: green means proven with no failure; failures means at least one confirmed failure; blocked means the run stopped; unproven means the new behaviour was not shown; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
verdict.question: How do runs end?

reason.measured_from: The reason in the child's blocked verdict line, or launch's own reason when the child printed no verdict line or launch refused.
reason.excludes: Reasons for runs that were not blocked.
reason.reading: A text names why the run stopped; null means the run was not blocked or no reason was given.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
reason.question: Why are runs blocked?

core.description: The core branch the run compares against.
core.measured_from: The --core flag lighthouse launch was given.
core.excludes: The commit, which the summary's core_commit records.
core.reading: A name identifies the branch; null means unknown.
core.question: Which core branch was the run proving against?

feature.description: The FEATURE branch the run proves.
feature.measured_from: The --feature flag lighthouse launch was given.
feature.excludes: The commit, which the summary's feature_commit records.
feature.reading: A name identifies the branch; null means unknown.
feature.question: Which FEATURE branch was the run proving?

core_commit.description: The core branch's commit the run tested.
core_commit.measured_from: The results folder's commits.json core entry.
core_commit.reading: An id names the commit; null means commits.json is missing, unreadable or holds no entry.
core_commit.question: Which core commit was tested?

feature_commit.description: The FEATURE branch's commit the run tested.
feature_commit.measured_from: The results folder's commits.json feature entry.
feature_commit.reading: An id names the commit; null means commits.json is missing, unreadable or holds no entry.
feature_commit.question: Which FEATURE commit was tested?

retest.description: Whether the run retests from previous results.
retest.includes: Runs given a previous results folder.
retest.reading: true means a retest; false means a fresh run; null means unknown.
retest.question: How often does a run retest from earlier results?

final.description: Whether the run was the final one before opening the pull request.
final.reading: true means the run was final; false means it was not; null means unknown.
final.question: How often is a run the final one?

spec.description: Whether the run was given a spec to read.
spec.reading: true means a spec was given; false means none was; null means unknown.
spec.question: How often does a run have a spec?

failures.description: How many confirmed failures the verdict line lists.
failures.measured_from: The length of the failures list in the verdict line lighthouse launch prints.
failures.includes: Every entry of the line's failures list.
failures.reading: Higher means more confirmed failures; 0 means none; null means unknown.
failures.question: How many confirmed failures does a run report?

unproven.description: How many unproven paths the verdict line lists.
unproven.measured_from: The length of the unproven list in the verdict line lighthouse launch prints.
unproven.includes: Every entry of the line's unproven list.
unproven.reading: Higher means more unproven paths; 0 means none; null means unknown.
unproven.question: How many unproven paths does a run report?

flaky.description: How many flaky tests and paths the verdict line lists.
flaky.measured_from: The length of the flaky list in the verdict line lighthouse launch prints.
flaky.includes: Every entry of the line's flaky list.
flaky.reading: Higher means more flaky tests and paths; 0 means none; null means unknown.
flaky.question: How many flaky tests and paths does a run report?

build.description: Whether FEATURE built for product testing.
build.includes: The build result and its reason.
build.excludes: The suite's own builds, which suite records.
build.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes; null means findings.json is missing or unreadable.
build.question: How often does FEATURE fail to build for product testing?

result.reading: ok means it built; blocked means it did not; null means unknown.
result.question: Did FEATURE build for product testing?

reason.description: Why the FEATURE build was blocked.
reason.includes: The reason text the child session gave.
reason.reading: A text names the cause; null means none was given or it is unknown.
reason.question: Why does FEATURE fail to build?

suite.description: The project's own suite run on both builds.
suite.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json, written by lighthouse suite.
suite.includes: The suite's result and reason, the counts of its failures, pre-existing failures and flaky tests, and each build's timings.
suite.excludes: The test ids, logs and the suite command.
suite.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes; null means suite.json is missing or unreadable.
suite.question: Did the project's suite run on both branches, and what did it find?

result.includes: One of passed, failures or blocked.
result.excludes: The product paths, which paths records.
result.reading: passed means no FEATURE failure; failures means at least one confirmed failure; blocked means the suite could not run; null means unknown.
result.question: How often does the suite pass, fail or stop?

reason.description: Why the suite stopped or has no core baseline.
reason.reading: A text names the cause; null means none was given or it is unknown.
reason.question: Why does the suite stop or run without a baseline?

failures.description: How many tests failed on FEATURE and were confirmed as failures.
failures.measured_from: The length of the results folder's suite.json failures list.
failures.includes: Tests that failed on FEATURE twice and did not fail on core.
failures.reading: Higher means more confirmed suite failures; 0 means none; null means unknown.
failures.question: How many suite failures does a FEATURE branch carry?

pre_existing.description: How many tests failed on both builds.
pre_existing.measured_from: The length of the results folder's suite.json pre_existing list.
pre_existing.includes: Tests that failed on FEATURE and also on core.
pre_existing.reading: Higher means more failures the core branch already had; 0 means none; null means unknown.
pre_existing.question: How many failures come from the core branch rather than the change?

flaky.description: How many tests failed once and passed on their rerun.
flaky.measured_from: The length of the results folder's suite.json flaky list.
flaky.includes: Tests whose FEATURE result changed between the first run and the rerun.
flaky.reading: Higher means more tests changed result between runs; 0 means none; null means unknown.
flaky.question: How flaky is the project's suite?

core.description: The suite timings of the core build.
core.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json entry for the core build, its minutes times 60.
core.includes: Preparation, first run and rerun seconds, and whether the result was reused.
core.excludes: The test ids and the suite log.
core.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes; null means suite.json holds no entry for this build.
core.question: Where does the suite spend its time on the core build?

prepare_seconds.description: How long preparing the build took before its suite ran.
prepare_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json prepare_minutes for the build, times 60.
prepare_seconds.includes: Setup and build commands the profile names for that build.
prepare_seconds.excludes: The suite run itself and any rerun.
prepare_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
prepare_seconds.question: How long does preparing each build take?

suite_seconds.description: How long the build's first suite run took.
suite_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json suite_minutes for the build, times 60.
suite_seconds.includes: The first run of the project's own suite on that build.
suite_seconds.excludes: Preparation and any rerun of failed tests.
suite_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
suite_seconds.question: How long does the project's suite take on each build?

rerun_seconds.description: How long rerunning the build's failed tests took.
rerun_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json rerun_minutes for the build, times 60.
rerun_seconds.includes: The rerun of tests that failed on the first run.
rerun_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
rerun_seconds.question: How much time do reruns of failed tests add?

reused.description: Whether the build's stored suite result was reused instead of running the suite again.
reused.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json reused flag for the build.
reused.includes: A core result stored by an earlier run at the same commit and suite settings.
reused.excludes: A FEATURE build, which is never reused.
reused.reading: true means the stored result was reused and no suite ran; false means the suite ran; null means unknown.
reused.question: How often does a run reuse core's stored suite result?

feature.description: The suite timings of the FEATURE build.
feature.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json entry for the FEATURE build, its minutes times 60.
feature.includes: Preparation, first run and rerun seconds, and whether the result was reused.
feature.excludes: The test ids and the suite log.
feature.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes; null means suite.json holds no entry for this build.
feature.question: Where does the suite spend its time on the FEATURE build?

prepare_seconds.description: How long preparing the build took before its suite ran.
prepare_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json prepare_minutes for the build, times 60.
prepare_seconds.includes: Setup and build commands the profile names for that build.
prepare_seconds.excludes: The suite run itself and any rerun.
prepare_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
prepare_seconds.question: How long does preparing each build take?

suite_seconds.description: How long the build's first suite run took.
suite_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json suite_minutes for the build, times 60.
suite_seconds.includes: The first run of the project's own suite on that build.
suite_seconds.excludes: Preparation and any rerun of failed tests.
suite_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
suite_seconds.question: How long does the project's suite take on each build?

rerun_seconds.description: How long rerunning the build's failed tests took.
rerun_seconds.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json rerun_minutes for the build, times 60.
rerun_seconds.includes: The rerun of tests that failed on the first run.
rerun_seconds.reading: Higher means longer; 0 means no time was recorded; null means unknown.
rerun_seconds.question: How much time do reruns of failed tests add?

reused.description: Whether the build's stored suite result was reused instead of running the suite again.
reused.measured_from: The results folder's suite.json reused flag for the build.
reused.includes: A core result stored by an earlier run at the same commit and suite settings.
reused.excludes: A FEATURE build, which is never reused.
reused.reading: true means the stored result was reused and no suite ran; false means the suite ran; null means unknown.
reused.question: How often does a run reuse core's stored suite result?

paths.description: The product paths the run checked.
paths.measured_from: The results folder's findings.json paths, with carried from retest.json carried_paths.
paths.includes: Every new behaviour and neighbour path in findings.json.
paths.reading: Each item reads as its entries describe; an empty list means no path was checked; null means findings.json is missing or unreadable.
paths.question: Which product paths were driven or rechecked, and how did each end?

items.description: One product path the run checked.
items.measured_from: One entry of the results folder's findings.json paths.
items.includes: The path's name, kind, status, check, retry and whether it was carried.
items.excludes: The path's evidence, surface and expected behaviour.
items.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes.
items.question: What happened to each product path?

name.includes: The name the run gave the path.
name.excludes: The surface the path belongs to.
name.reading: A name identifies the path within the run; null means unknown.
name.question: Which product path is this?

kind.description: Whether the path is new behaviour or a neighbour of the change.
kind.includes: new for behaviour the change adds, neighbour for a surface next to the change.
kind.reading: new means the change adds this behaviour; neighbour means it is rechecked beside the change; null means unknown.
kind.question: How many new behaviours and neighbours does a run check?

status.includes: passed, failed or unproven on the FEATURE build.
status.excludes: The retry and the core result.
status.reading: passed means it behaved as expected; failed means it did not; unproven means it was not shown either way; null means unknown.
status.question: How often are product paths proven?

check.measured_from: The kind of the path's check in findings.json.
check.includes: suite for an existing test, direct for a direct call, drive for driving the running product.
check.excludes: The reason the check was chosen.
check.reading: suite, direct and drive name the check used; null means the path carries no check, such as a carried path.
check.question: How are product paths checked?

retry.description: The result of the path's retry after a failure.
retry.includes: passed or failed on the retry.
retry.excludes: The first attempt, which status records.
retry.reading: passed means the retry passed; failed means it failed again; null means there was no retry or it is unknown.
retry.question: How often does a failed path pass on retry?

carried.description: Whether the path was carried from previous results rather than checked again.
carried.measured_from: Whether the path is among the results folder's retest.json carried_paths.
carried.includes: Paths a retest carried over unchanged.
carried.excludes: Paths driven again in this run.
carried.reading: true means the result was carried from an earlier run; false means it was checked in this run; null means unknown.
carried.question: How much of a retest is carried rather than checked again?

usd.description: The US dollars of the run's own spend, priced at write time.
usd.measured_from: Every assistant message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span, counted once by message id, priced by exact model id with lighthouse_tool/prices.json read when launch writes the summary.
usd.includes: Every counted message of the run's own spend in all five token kinds.
usd.excludes: Any message outside the run's own spend.
usd.reading: Higher means more dollars spent; 0 means no counted tokens; null means a counted model has no price or the spend is unknown. It is lighthouse's own spend only, every message of the run counted once; a whole pipeline run's cost is the sum of usd over its run tree.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
usd.question: What did the run's own spend cost?

price_date.description: The date of the price table the run was priced from.
price_date.measured_from: The date of lighthouse_tool/prices.json when launch wrote the summary.
price_date.reading: A later date means a newer price table; null means the table carried no date or the run was imported.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
price_date.question: Which prices produced usd?

tokens.description: The tokens of the run's own spend in the five kinds.
tokens.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block, by kind.
tokens.includes: The five token kinds input, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, cache_read and output.
tokens.excludes: Any token a message's usage block does not report.
tokens.reading: Each kind is a count of tokens; higher means more tokens of that kind; all zero means no counted message; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
tokens.question: Which kinds of tokens make up the run's own spend?

input.description: The fresh input tokens, read without a cache of the run's own spend.
input.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block.
input.includes: Every fresh input tokens, read without a cache counted in the run's own spend.
input.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
input.reading: A higher count means more fresh input tokens, read without a cache; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
input.question: How many fresh input tokens, read without a cache did the run's own spend take?

cache_write_5m.description: The input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes of the run's own spend.
cache_write_5m.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block.
cache_write_5m.includes: Every input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes counted in the run's own spend.
cache_write_5m.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_write_5m.reading: A higher count means more input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_write_5m.question: How many input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes did the run's own spend take?

cache_write_1h.description: The input tokens written to a cache kept one hour of the run's own spend.
cache_write_1h.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block.
cache_write_1h.includes: Every input tokens written to a cache kept one hour counted in the run's own spend.
cache_write_1h.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_write_1h.reading: A higher count means more input tokens written to a cache kept one hour; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_write_1h.question: How many input tokens written to a cache kept one hour did the run's own spend take?

cache_read.description: The input tokens read from a cache of the run's own spend.
cache_read.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block.
cache_read.includes: Every input tokens read from a cache counted in the run's own spend.
cache_read.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_read.reading: A higher count means more input tokens read from a cache; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_read.question: How many input tokens read from a cache did the run's own spend take?

output.description: The output tokens the model wrote of the run's own spend.
output.measured_from: Summed over every counted message of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span from each message's usage block.
output.includes: Every output tokens the model wrote counted in the run's own spend.
output.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
output.reading: A higher count means more output tokens the model wrote; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
output.question: How many output tokens the model wrote did the run's own spend take?

messages.description: How many assistant messages the run counted.
messages.measured_from: The assistant messages of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span, counted once by message id.
messages.includes: Messages of the child session, its drivers, its trial sessions and the caller inside the span.
messages.excludes: Messages before run.start, caller messages after run.end and repeated message ids.
messages.reading: Higher means more model turns; 0 means none were found; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
messages.question: How many model turns does a run take?

models.description: The run's spend by exact model id.
models.measured_from: The counted messages of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span, grouped by model.
models.includes: One item per model seen in the counted messages.
models.reading: Each item reads as its entries describe; an empty list means no message was counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
models.question: Which models does a run use?

items.description: One model's share of the run's spend.
items.measured_from: The counted messages of the transcripts under the results folder and the caller's transcript inside the run's span grouped by exact model id.
items.includes: The model id, its tokens and its dollars.
items.excludes: Other models, which have their own entries.
items.reading: Each key reads as its own entry describes.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
items.question: Which models does a run use, and what does each cost?

model.measured_from: The model of each counted message.
model.includes: The id as the transcript records it.
model.excludes: Family names, which are never used.
model.reading: An id names one model; unknown names messages without a model; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
model.question: Which model is this?

tokens.description: The tokens of the model's messages in the five kinds.
tokens.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block, by kind.
tokens.includes: The five token kinds input, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, cache_read and output.
tokens.excludes: Any token a message's usage block does not report.
tokens.reading: Each kind is a count of tokens; higher means more tokens of that kind; all zero means no counted message; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
tokens.question: Which kinds of tokens make up the model's messages?

input.description: The fresh input tokens, read without a cache of the model's messages.
input.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block.
input.includes: Every fresh input tokens, read without a cache counted in the model's messages.
input.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
input.reading: A higher count means more fresh input tokens, read without a cache; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
input.question: How many fresh input tokens, read without a cache did the model's messages take?

cache_write_5m.description: The input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes of the model's messages.
cache_write_5m.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block.
cache_write_5m.includes: Every input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes counted in the model's messages.
cache_write_5m.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_write_5m.reading: A higher count means more input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_write_5m.question: How many input tokens written to a cache kept five minutes did the model's messages take?

cache_write_1h.description: The input tokens written to a cache kept one hour of the model's messages.
cache_write_1h.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block.
cache_write_1h.includes: Every input tokens written to a cache kept one hour counted in the model's messages.
cache_write_1h.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_write_1h.reading: A higher count means more input tokens written to a cache kept one hour; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_write_1h.question: How many input tokens written to a cache kept one hour did the model's messages take?

cache_read.description: The input tokens read from a cache of the model's messages.
cache_read.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block.
cache_read.includes: Every input tokens read from a cache counted in the model's messages.
cache_read.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
cache_read.reading: A higher count means more input tokens read from a cache; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
cache_read.question: How many input tokens read from a cache did the model's messages take?

output.description: The output tokens the model wrote of the model's messages.
output.measured_from: Summed over the counted messages of that model from each message's usage block.
output.includes: Every output tokens the model wrote counted in the model's messages.
output.excludes: Every other token kind, which has its own key.
output.reading: A higher count means more output tokens the model wrote; 0 means none were counted; null means unknown.
readers: a harness reading its child runs
output.question: How many output tokens the model wrote did the model's messages take?

usd.description: The US dollars of the model's messages, priced at write time.
usd.measured_from: The counted messages of that model, priced by exact model id with lighthouse_tool/prices.json read when launch writes the summary.
usd.includes: Every counted message of the model's messages in all five token kinds.
usd.excludes: Any message outside the model's messages.
usd.reading: Higher means more dollars spent; 0 means no counted tokens; null means a counted model has no price or the spend is unknown.

queries.name: verdicts
queries.question: How do lighthouse runs end?
queries.sql: SELECT verdict, count(*) AS runs FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse' GROUP BY verdict ORDER BY runs DESC, verdict

queries.name: spend
queries.question: What does each lighthouse run cost in money and time, newest first?
queries.sql: SELECT run, usd, run_seconds FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse' ORDER BY started DESC, run

queries.name: steps
queries.question: Where do lighthouse runs spend time and money by step?
queries.sql: SELECT s.step AS step, sum(s.elapsed_seconds) AS elapsed_seconds, sum(s.usd) AS usd FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(to_json(steps), '[{"step":"VARCHAR","build":"VARCHAR","elapsed_seconds":"DOUBLE","usd":"DOUBLE"}]')) AS s FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse') GROUP BY s.step ORDER BY elapsed_seconds DESC NULLS LAST, step

queries.name: paths
queries.question: How do the product paths lighthouse checks end, by kind and check?
queries.sql: SELECT p.kind AS kind, p.status AS status, p."check" AS "check", count(*) AS paths FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(to_json(paths), '[{"kind":"VARCHAR","status":"VARCHAR","check":"VARCHAR"}]')) AS p FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse') GROUP BY p.kind, p.status, p."check" ORDER BY paths DESC, kind, status, "check"

queries.name: suite
queries.question: How long does the project's suite take on each build of each run, and was core's result reused?
queries.sql: SELECT run, build, suite_seconds, reused FROM (SELECT run, started, 'core' AS build, from_json(to_json(suite), '{"core":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"},"feature":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"}}').core.suite_seconds AS suite_seconds, from_json(to_json(suite), '{"core":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"},"feature":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"}}').core.reused AS reused FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse' UNION ALL SELECT run, started, 'feature' AS build, from_json(to_json(suite), '{"core":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"},"feature":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"}}').feature.suite_seconds AS suite_seconds, from_json(to_json(suite), '{"core":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"},"feature":{"suite_seconds":"DOUBLE","reused":"BOOLEAN"}}').feature.reused AS reused FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse') ORDER BY started DESC, run, build

queries.name: blocked
queries.question: Why are lighthouse runs blocked?
queries.sql: SELECT reason, count(*) AS runs FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'lighthouse' AND verdict = 'blocked' GROUP BY reason ORDER BY runs DESC, reason
